## Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

![Asian giant softshell turtle photo 1](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pelochelys_cantorii.jpg)  
*Photo: Wikimedia Commons*

![Asian giant softshell turtle photo 2](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cantor%27s_Giant_Softshell_Turtle.jpg)  
*Photo: Wikimedia Commons*

The Asian giant softshell turtle, also called Cantor’s giant softshell turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), is one of the largest freshwater turtles in the world. It can grow over three feet long and has a flat, leathery shell instead of the hard, bony shell that many turtles have. Its soft body and wide head help it blend into sandy or muddy river bottoms, where it spends much of its time buried and waiting for prey.

This turtle lives in parts of South and Southeast Asia, including rivers and wetlands in countries such as India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia. It is mostly aquatic and rarely comes onto land except when females lay eggs. The Asian giant softshell turtle is a carnivore, eating fish, crustaceans, mollusks, and other small aquatic animals. It is an ambush predator, meaning it hides quietly and strikes quickly when food comes close.

Unfortunately, this species is in serious danger. The International Union for Conservation of Nature lists it as Critically Endangered. Major threats include habitat destruction, river pollution, fishing nets, egg collection, and hunting for meat. Dams and changes to river systems also harm the sandy nesting areas that females need. Because the turtle is shy and spends so much time hidden underwater, scientists still do not know everything about its behavior or population size.

Conservation groups are working to protect nesting sites, reduce hunting, and study the species more closely. Protecting healthy rivers is important not only for the Asian giant softshell turtle, but also for many other animals and people who depend on freshwater ecosystems.

“Cantor’s Giant Softshell Turtle.” *Turtle Survival Alliance*, turtlesurvival.org.
